# gbmc-pacemaker / pacemaker_fuzzer

OSS-Fuzz's fuzz target `pacemaker_fuzzer` ([source](source/pacemaker_fuzzer.cc), unmodified) over gbmcweb (gbmc.googlesource.com/gbmcweb at 7c20d387).

Creates a tlbmc Pacemaker whose ShellCommandExecutor returns fuzz-chosen strings or InternalError, then calls PerformChecks, GetMonitoringData, GetPid/GetCpuUsage/GetLastActiveTimestamp/IsServiceActive/RestartService on a fuzzed process name, IsPortListening, GetMemoryUsage and RecordError; every result is cast to (void).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against gbmcweb at commit 7c20d387.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

**Some statements are blocked by the model.** On the inputs they cover, the binary uses epoll or eventfd, opens files other than its input and starts threads, which this release's model does not decode, so the statements marked "blocked by the model" are false in this model for that reason alone. The program is not at fault.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch gbmc-pacemaker` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `pacemaker_fuzzer.plain` | 1,079,136 | `df382c5a4c3c0f12ba1644b5f9bbe612be79a65866d68c85c340237fbe94788a` |
| ubsan | `pacemaker_fuzzer.ubsan` | 1,148,632 | `6c2eed9526cfbd85cc8eaf8d316913586a40064aca451b44920519183157ac65` |
| asan | `pacemaker_fuzzer.asan` | 2,234,576 | `32d644aa3a7aeded0536fbf311f19875163efe5c9b1825b01b38d630b1f6ff5c` |
| asan-ubsan | `pacemaker_fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 2,296,784 | `9e3bd979d1914893d6c98f3e9bec81aa9039202d9564c4171d89e7644f1c137d` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
